clue.text: Aged catch, with head displaying aloof manner

indicators.note: with means one piece accompanies the next, so they are set side by side

parts.note: as in a man of eighty, of can mean aged
to fish is to try to catch
a ness is a headland

explanation.surface: An elderly angler, nose in the air, holds up the day's catch with a superior air.
explanation.definitionFit: Being offish means standing coldly apart from others, so offishness is a distant, standoffish bearing.

clue.text: By the sound of it, make bacon from a pig in liqueur

indicators.note: the phrase asks the solver to judge the words by how they are spoken, not spelt

parts.note: to cure pork is to make bacon of it, and a sow is a female pig

explanation.surface: A recipe for turning a pig into bacon steeped in a liqueur.
explanation.definitionFit: Curacao is an orange-flavoured liqueur named after the Caribbean island where its bitter oranges grow.

clue.text: Quickly insert something to repair tap after start of seepage

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of seepage
to patch something is to repair it
a cock is a tap or valve, as in stopcock

explanation.surface: A plumber's instruction: patch up a leaking tap once the seepage starts.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue order puts the start of seepage last, but after tells you it leads the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To spatchcock is to interpolate hastily, to force an extra passage into a text or speech in a hurry.

clue.text: Resort to spot on end of peak

indicators.note: in a down clue on means sitting above, so the first part stands on top of the second

parts.note: to spot something is to see it

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, the only one kept here

parts.note: the final letter of peak

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker heads for a resort to admire the view from the top of a peak.
explanation.walkthrough: Resort looks like a holiday place, but it is a verb: to resort to something.
explanation.definitionFit: To seek, in an older sense, is to go to or have recourse to, which is what resorting to means.

clue.text: Fish oil painter's used liberally

indicators.note: something used liberally is splashed about freely, so these letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: the possessive supplies its S as a letter

explanation.surface: An artist slaps on a fish-based oil medium with abandon.
explanation.definitionFit: Pristane is a hydrocarbon found in shark-liver and other fish oils, so the clue names it by its source.

clue.text: S. Indians in formal garb around start of mela

indicators.note: around means the outfit wraps itself round the other piece

parts.note: tails are a formal tailcoat

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, the only one kept

parts.note: the opening letter of mela

explanation.surface: South Indians in evening dress gather at the start of a festival.
explanation.walkthrough: A mela is a South Asian fair or festival, which fits the scene but gives just one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tamils are a people of southern India and Sri Lanka, so they are South Indians.

clue.text: Nashgab, smart, one supplanting English

indicators.note: to supplant is to oust and take the place of, so one letter swaps in for another

parts.note: smart means clever
a, the indefinite article, means one
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A clever talker is cast as a chatterbox who replaced an Englishman.
explanation.walkthrough: Nashgab is Scots for prattle or chatter; claver is a Scots word for idle talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Claver is Scottish gossip or idle chatter, the same as the Scots nashgab.

clue.text: Suffer with relative whom locals regard as a fool

definitions.text: whom locals regard as a fool

indicators.note: with means one piece comes along beside the next, so they join end to end

parts.note: to have an illness is to suffer it
rel is the abbreviation for relative

explanation.surface: Someone puts up with a relative the neighbours think is an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: Locals signals a regional word: haverel is Scots, from haver, to talk nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: A haverel is a half-witted or foolish person in Scottish dialect, one who havers or babbles.

clue.text: Poet's just close to cathedral city

parts.note: on can mean near or beside, as in a town on the coast
Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: A poet settles down not far from a cathedral city.
explanation.walkthrough: Poet's flags a poetic word: onely is Spenser's spelling of only.
explanation.definitionFit: Just in the sense merely or only; onely is the old poetic spelling of only.

clue.text: 50% of state leaving for spiritual leader

indicators.note: half the state's name departs, so only the front half survives

parts.note: California is a US state, ten letters long

explanation.surface: Half a state's people leave to follow a spiritual guru.
explanation.definitionFit: A calif, or caliph, is the successor of Muhammad as religious and civil head of the Muslim community.

clue.text: Constitution of EU modified with inclusion of short rule

indicators.note: inclusion means one piece is taken inside the other
something modified has been altered, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for rule

explanation.surface: Talk of amending the European Union's constitution to add a brief rule.
explanation.walkthrough: Of looks like a link joining Constitution to EU, but it is part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A fuero is a Spanish charter or code of privileges granted to a town or province, a kind of constitution.

clue.text: My child, a girl (not Di) coming after a boy

indicators.note: coming after places the girl's part behind the boy's

parts.note: Alan is a boy's name

indicators.note: not marks the bracketed name as something to take away

parts.note: Dinah is a girl's name
taken as written

explanation.surface: A parent speaks of their child, a daughter (not called Di) born after a son.
explanation.definitionFit: Alannah is an Irish endearment, from a leanbh, meaning my child, said to a son or daughter.

clue.text: Ref punished Italian, a warning, ye ken

indicators.note: something punished has been knocked about, so these letters are beaten into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
It is the abbreviation for Italian

explanation.surface: A referee books an Italian player and gives him a warning, Scottish style.
explanation.walkthrough: Ye ken, Scots for you know, flags a Scottish word.
explanation.definitionFit: A freit is a Scots word for an omen or portent, a sign that warns of what is to come.

clue.text: Source of rennet, contents of level ladle

indicators.note: the contents are what lies inside, so the letters sit within the next words

parts.note: taken from inside the two words, across the gap

explanation.surface: A cheesemaker measures out a level ladleful of rennet.
explanation.definitionFit: The vell is the fourth stomach of a calf, from which rennet for cheesemaking is taken.

clue.text: What can make line curl at being twisted double-convex

indicators.note: twisting bends things out of their original shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A question about what bends a straight line into a curved lens shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Lenticular means shaped like a lentil or lens, bulging outward on both faces.

clue.text: Evil, devious foreigner mostly getting to conceal shameful deeds (8, three words)

indicators.note: something devious takes a winding, crooked path, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: mostly means all but a bit, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: an alien is a foreigner

explanation.surface: A wicked, scheming outsider manages to hide his disgraceful past.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the phrase LIVE A LIE.
explanation.definitionFit: To live a lie is to keep up a false front, hiding the shameful truth about oneself.

clue.text: Sink? It's often by the fire

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to sink a ship deliberately by holing it
second meaning: a coal bucket kept by the hearth

explanation.walkthrough: Sink looks like a kitchen sink, but it is the verb, as in sinking one's own ship.
explanation.definitionFit: To scuttle a ship is to sink it on purpose, and a coal scuttle is the pail kept beside the fireplace.

clue.text: He's among group having to hurry over leaflet

indicators.note: in a down clue over means placed above, so this part comes first

parts.note: to fly is to rush

indicators.note: among puts one piece in the midst of the other

parts.note: a set is a group
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man in a group must hurry to hand out a leaflet.
explanation.definitionFit: A flysheet is a single printed sheet handed out, the same as a leaflet or handbill.

clue.text: Bother keeps besetting head

indicators.note: to beset is to surround on all sides, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: someone who keeps a thing has it
a ras is a headland or cape

explanation.surface: A nagging worry keeps nagging at someone's head.
explanation.walkthrough: Ras, Arabic for head, appears in names of capes such as Ras Tanura.
explanation.definitionFit: To harass someone is to pester or trouble them repeatedly, which is to bother them.

clue.text: Grease applied to help old siren?

indicators.note: applied to means one piece is put next to the other

parts.note: seam is an old word for grease or lard
aid means help

explanation.surface: A query whether a dab of grease would help an aged temptress.
explanation.definitionFit: A seamaid is an archaic name for a mermaid, the sea-dwelling siren who lures sailors.

clue.text: Hold back old cur let out

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An owner restrains an old dog that has been let out.
explanation.walkthrough: Old marks the answer as an archaic word.
explanation.definitionFit: Reluct is an old verb meaning to struggle against or resist, to hold back reluctantly.

clue.text: Evening of music etc from Spain I cover in church

indicators.note: in places the preceding pieces inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: CH is the abbreviation for church
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)
taken as written
a lid is a cover

explanation.surface: A Spanish visitor provides cover for a music night held in church.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceilidh is a Scottish or Irish social evening of folk music, dancing and storytelling.

clue.text: Quickie during lunch break? Not a soul having run!

indicators.note: having means taking on something extra, which is attached at the end

parts.note: not a soul means nobody
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A lunchtime tryst with nobody around, then a quick dash back.
explanation.definitionFit: A nooner is slang for sex at midday, a quick encounter squeezed into the lunch hour.

clue.text: Former kick, if delivered by Old Nick coming up on one's rear end

indicators.note: in a down clue on means sitting above the next piece
in a down clue coming up means read from bottom to top
delivered by means released from, so those two letters are set free of the name

parts.note: Old Nick and Lucifer are both names for the Devil
taken as written

indicators.note: the rear end of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of one

explanation.surface: The Devil delivers a kick to someone's backside.
explanation.walkthrough: Former marks an archaic word: recule is an old form of recoil.
explanation.definitionFit: A recule is the backward kick of a gun when fired, an old form of recoil.

clue.text: First sign of cockroaches — I yelp frenziedly, insect protectors needed

indicators.note: the first sign of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of cockroaches

indicators.note: in a frenzy things fly about wildly, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone spots a cockroach, screams in panic and reaches for protection.
explanation.definitionFit: Clypei, plural of clypeus, are the shield-like plates on the front of an insect's head.

clue.text: Trader, one invited in by late-lamented funny man?

indicators.note: a guest invited in ends up inside the host, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: Barry Cryer, the British comedian and comedy writer, died in January 2022
a, the indefinite article, means one

explanation.surface: A merchant asks whether he is the one a much-missed comedian invited in.
explanation.definitionFit: A crayer was a small trading vessel, so a trader in the sense of a merchant ship.

clue.text: Ecclesiastic gown moved gradually and rustled

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a long vestment worn by a priest
second meaning: crept slowly and quietly
third meaning: took cattle or other animals by theft

explanation.surface: A priest's robe swished softly along as it moved.
explanation.walkthrough: Rustled sounds like the swish of the gown, but it means stealing livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: Three senses of one word: a clerical vestment, the past tense of steal as creep, and the past tense of steal as thieve.

clue.text: Dry up after ten? Try a sherry

indicators.note: after means this part follows the other

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral for ten

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: sere means dry or withered

explanation.surface: After ten in the evening, dry up and try a glass of sherry.
explanation.definitionFit: Xeres is the old name of Jerez, the Andalusian town that gave sherry its name, and so the wine itself.

clue.text: Argumentative type is tense when restricted by fine

indicators.note: something restricted is hemmed in, so it ends up inside the other piece

parts.note: an eric was a blood-fine paid for murder in old Irish law
taken as written
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A quarrelsome sort pays a fine, and the mood turns tense.
explanation.definitionFit: An eristic is someone given to disputation, a person who argues for the sake of winning.

clue.text: One answer to air pollution making mark, involving collaborative group? (8, two words)

indicators.note: involving means wrapping in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a scar is a mark left on the skin
a team is a group working together

explanation.surface: A query whether a cooperative group could make a dent in air pollution.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is two words, STEAM CAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A steam car burns fuel outside the engine more cleanly than petrol cars, so it is proposed as a remedy for exhaust fumes.

clue.text: Scottish supernumerary from among junior ranks

indicators.note: taken from among the following words, the letters lie inside them

parts.note: taken from inside the two words, across the gap

explanation.surface: A spare Scottish soldier is picked out of the lower ranks.
explanation.definitionFit: Orra is Scots for odd or spare, left over beyond the usual number, which is what supernumerary means.

clue.text: Flock of ducks, mute? Not one duck

indicators.note: not one says a single letter of the word must go

parts.note: sordo is an Italian musical term for muted
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A puzzled question whether a flock of ducks is silent, with one duck missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Duck appears twice: the first is the bird of the definition, the second the cricketer's zero.
explanation.definitionFit: A sord is a flight or flock of mallards, a collective noun for wild ducks.

clue.text: Counter for game? Learner must join club

indicators.note: join means link up, so the two pieces are joined end to end

parts.note: a meri is a short Maori war club
L is the learner-driver abbreviation

explanation.surface: A newcomer wondering what to play with is told to join a games club.
explanation.walkthrough: The club comes first in the answer even though learner is named first.
explanation.definitionFit: A meril is a counter or piece used in the old board game merels, also called nine men's morris.

clue.text: Law kept in line? It's not rigid across the water

indicators.note: something kept in is held inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a file is a line of people one behind another
lex is Latin for law

explanation.surface: A question whether the law is kept in check, with the answer that it is pliable overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: Across the water flags an American usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Flexile means bending easily, the opposite of stiff, a word recorded as chiefly American.

clue.text: Fox found in Zambia, form of red one

parts.note: Z is the international vehicle code for Zambia

indicators.note: a form of something is a reshaped version, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: red as written, and one as A

explanation.surface: A fox found in Zambia turns out to be a reddish type.
explanation.definitionFit: The zerda is the fennec, a small desert fox of North Africa with very large ears.

clue.text: Requirements

parts.note: the bare definition of the competition word
in a plain competition puzzle solvers write this clue themselves, so only a definition is printed

explanation.walkthrough: This was the competition word: Azed gives only a definition, and entrants submit their own cryptic clue for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Desiderata, Latin for things desired, are the things needed or wanted, so essential requirements.
